question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

53, 111, 227, 459, 923, 1851, ?, 7419
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 3707.

GIVEN

• 53, 111, 227, 459, 923, 1851, ?, 7419

SOLUTION

• The rule is ×2 + 5 each time.

• 53×2+5 = 111; 111×2+5 = 227; 227×2+5 = 459; 459×2+5 = 923; 923×2+5 = 1851.

• Missing term = 1851×2+5 = 3707 (check: 3707×2+5 = 7419).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Each next number is roughly double the previous; double 1851 and add 5 → 3707 (matches the given 7419 that follows).

NOTE

• For number series always test the pattern aⁿ = a×2+k, ×3±k etc.; verifying it fits the LAST given term confirms the rule.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

U, S, Q, O, M, ?, I, G
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. K.

GIVEN

• U, S, Q, O, M, ?, I, G

SOLUTION

• Positions: U=21, S=19, Q=17, O=15, M=13, then G=7, I=9 further down.

• Each letter decreases by 2: 21, 19, 17, 15, 13, 11, 9, 7.

• Position 11 = K.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Alternate alphabet going backwards (skip one letter): U S Q O M K I G.

NOTE

• Memorise letter positions (A=1 … Z=26); a constant −2 step is the commonest single-letter series pattern.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

WY, YZ, AB, CE, EI, GN, ?, KA
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. IT.

GIVEN

• WY, YZ, AB, CE, EI, GN, ?, KA

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: W, Y, A, C, E, G, ?, K → each +2 (23,25,1,3,5,7,9=I,11). So 1st letter = I.

• 2nd letters: Y, Z, B, E, I, N, ?, A → gaps +1,+2,+3,+4,+5,+6,+7 (25,26,2,5,9,14,20=T,1). So 2nd letter = T.

• Missing term = IT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Split into two columns: first letters jump +2 (→I); second letters jump by an increasing count (…N +6→ T).

NOTE

• In two-letter series solve each position independently; watch for a constant step in one and an increasing step in the other.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

DJ : AC :: RN : OG :: LK : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ID.

GIVEN

• DJ : AC :: RN : OG :: LK : ?

SOLUTION

• DJ→AC: D(4)−3=A(1), J(10)−7=C(3).

• RN→OG: R(18)−3=O(15), N(14)−7=G(7). Same rule (−3, −7).

• LK→?: L(12)−3=I(9), K(11)−7=D(4) → ID.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter −3, second letter −7; apply to LK → I and D.

NOTE

• Fix the two shifts from any verified pair, then apply the same shifts to the target cluster.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

YJ : VE :: IO : ? :: SX : PS
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. FJ.

GIVEN

• YJ : VE :: IO : ? :: SX : PS

SOLUTION

• YJ→VE: Y(25)−3=V(22), J(10)−5=E(5).

• SX→PS: S(19)−3=P(16), X(24)−5=S(19). Same rule (−3, −5).

• IO→?: I(9)−3=F(6), O(15)−5=J(10) → FJ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter −3, second letter −5; IO → F and J.

NOTE

• Confirm the shift on the fully-given pair (SX:PS) before applying it to the unknown.

question: What was the day of the week on 25 December 2017?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Monday.

GIVEN

• Find the day of the week on 25 December 2017.

SOLUTION

• Odd days up to 2016 (complete years) + days of 2017 give the day.

• Easier: 1 January 2018 was a Monday; 25 December 2017 is exactly 7 days earlier, so it is the same weekday.

• Hence 25 December 2017 = Monday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Anchor to a nearby known date (1 Jan 2018 = Monday) and count in weeks: −7 days = same day = Monday.

NOTE

• Calendar rule: 100 yr = 5 odd days, 400 yr = 0; a known anchor date shortcuts the whole odd-day count.

question: If 16 May 2024 is a Wednesday, then what day will 6 October 2024 be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Saturday.

GIVEN

• 16 May 2024 = Wednesday. Find the day on 6 October 2024.

SOLUTION

• Days from 16 May to 6 Oct: May 15 + June 30 + July 31 + Aug 31 + Sep 30 + Oct 6 = 143 days.

• 143 ÷ 7 = 20 remainder 3 odd days.

• Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the remainder matters: 143 mod 7 = 3, so shift 3 days ahead of Wednesday → Saturday.

NOTE

• Count remaining days of the start month first, then add full months; take total mod 7 for the day shift.

question: A person was born on 8 June 2011. What day of the week will be on his 25th birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sunday.

GIVEN

• Date of birth 8 June 2011; find the weekday of the 25th birthday (8 June 2036).

SOLUTION

• 8 June 2011 was a Wednesday.

• Over 25 years, odd days = 25 + (number of leap days) = 25 + 7 (Feb-29s of 2012,16,20,24,28,32,36) = 32.

• 32 mod 7 = 4 odd days. Wednesday + 4 = Sunday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule: each year adds 1 odd day, each 29-Feb in between adds 1 more → 25+7 = 32 ≡ 4; Wed +4 = Sunday.

NOTE

• Count leap days by the number of Feb-29s falling strictly between the two matching dates (Feb-29 2036 counts as it precedes 8 June).

question: 5 boys J, R, M, B and C are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). R is to the immediate right of M. B is to the immediate left of M. J is to the right of R. C is to the left of M. How many boys are sitting to the left of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 0.

GIVEN

• 5 boys J, R, M, B, C in a row facing south. R = immediate right of M; B = immediate left of M; J = right of R; C = left of M.

SOLUTION

• From R right of M and B immediate-left of M: B M R.

• J is to the right of R: B M R J.

• C is to the left of M; B already sits immediate-left, so C goes further left: C B M R J.

• C is at the extreme left end, so no one is to its left → 0.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Place the immediate-left/right clues first (B M R), extend the ends; C lands leftmost → 0 boys to its left.

NOTE

• Keep 'left/right' consistent throughout for a facing-south row; the person's own left/right is used, not the reader's.

question: 7 girls P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). U sits second from left end of the row. R is third to the right of V. T sits third from right end of the row. R is to the immediate left of T. Q is fourth to the right of S. Who is sitting exactly in the middle of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. R.

GIVEN

• 7 girls facing north. U = 2nd from left; T = 3rd from right (position 5); R immediate-left of T (position 4); R = 3rd right of V; Q = 4th right of S.

SOLUTION

• Positions 1–7. T = 5, R = 4. R is 3rd right of V ⇒ V = 1. U = 2.

• Q is 4th right of S: with 3, 6, 7 left, S = 3 ⇒ Q = 7, leaving P = 6.

• Order: V, U, S, R, T, P, Q. Middle (position 4) = R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix T=5, R=4 first, back-solve V=1; the 'S…Q gap of 4' forces S=3,Q=7 → position 4 (middle) is R.

NOTE

• 'Middle of the row' in 7 seats is the 4th seat; nail down fixed-distance clues before the flexible ones.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the grid C J M / R □ / K D S.

GIVEN

• A 3×3 grid of letters/shapes changes to a second grid; apply the same change to the third grid.

SOLUTION

• The relation is a 90° clockwise rotation of the whole grid.

• Check on the first pair (A △ P / ◇ □ / T O L) → (T ✿ A / O △ / L □ P): rotating clockwise, the left column becomes the top row, etc. — it matches.

• Rotate the third grid (M □ S / J D / C R K) 90° clockwise → top row = C J M, middle = R □, bottom = K D S.

• This is exactly Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the left-most column of the given grid top-to-bottom (M, J, C) — after a clockwise turn it becomes the new top row read as C J M; that instantly points to Option 1.

NOTE

• For grid analogies test the four standard operations first: 90° CW, 90° ACW, 180°, and mirror — one of them almost always fits.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

GIVEN

• A box holds three symbols at top-left, centre and bottom-right; it changes to a second box. Apply the same change to the third box.

SOLUTION

• Rule: every symbol moves one place forward in the cycle top-left → centre → bottom-right → top-left, and at the same time each symbol is turned upside-down (180°).

• Check first pair: T (TL) → centre becomes ⊥; the corner (centre) → bottom-right becomes L; λ (BR) → top-left becomes Y. This gives the second box exactly.

• Third box (T top-left, pentagon centre, circle-stick bottom-right): T → centre = ⊥; pentagon → bottom-right = inverted pentagon; circle-stick → top-left = circle-on-top stick.

• Result = top-left circle-stick, centre ⊥, bottom-right inverted pentagon = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Track just one symbol: the top-left one lands in the centre flipped upside-down; only Option 3 shows the ⊥ (flipped T) in the middle.

NOTE

• When symbols keep their identity but change place and orientation, look for a positional cycle plus a fixed rotation applied to each element.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

XS520 : ? :: TP410 : MQ524 :: JT300 : QG414
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PU634.

GIVEN

• XS520 : ? :: TP410 : MQ524 :: JT300 : QG414

SOLUTION

• Letter rule: reverse the two letters and subtract 3 from each.

• TP410 → reverse PT → P−3=M, T−3=Q → MQ; JT300 → reverse TJ → T−3=Q, J−3=G → QG. Both fit.

• Number rule: +114 (410→524, 300→414).

• XS520 → reverse SX → S−3=P, X−3=U = PU; 520+114 = 634 → PU634.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Swap the letters, step each back by 3, and add 114 to the number → PU634.

NOTE

• If a straight shift fails, test 'reverse the letters then shift'; the number often changes by a fixed constant.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

KLO20 : ? :: MPS40 : OLI60 :: RTU80 : QPN120
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. KHG30.

GIVEN

• KLO20 : ? :: MPS40 : OLI60 :: RTU80 : QPN120

SOLUTION

• Letter rule: reverse the three letters and subtract 4 from each.

• MPS40 → reverse SPM → S−4=O, P−4=L, M−4=I → OLI; RTU80 → reverse UTR → U−4=Q, T−4=P, R−4=N → QPN. Both fit.

• Number rule: ×1.5 (40→60, 80→120).

• KLO20 → reverse OLK → O−4=K, L−4=H, K−4=G = KHG; 20×1.5 = 30 → KHG30.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the trio, drop each letter by 4, and multiply the number by 1.5 → KHG30.

NOTE

• Watch the number relation separately (here ×1.5); several options share the same number, so the letters decide the answer.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

3926 : ? :: 4189 : 4145 :: 8907 : 8863
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3882.

GIVEN

• 3926 : ? :: 4189 : 4145 :: 8907 : 8863

SOLUTION

• 4189 − 4145 = 44; 8907 − 8863 = 44. The rule is − 44.

• 3926 − 44 = 3882.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference of 44; subtract 44 from 3926 → 3882.

NOTE

• When two verified pairs differ by the same constant, apply that exact constant to the unknown pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

634 : 1907 :: ? : 119 :: 468 : 1409
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 38.

GIVEN

• 634 : 1907 :: ? : 119 :: 468 : 1409

SOLUTION

• Rule: number × 3 + 5. Check: 634×3+5 = 1907; 468×3+5 = 1409. Both fit.

• The option × 3 + 5 must give 119: so option = (119 − 5)/3 = 114/3 = 38.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule: (119 − 5) ÷ 3 = 38.

NOTE

• Here the second number is the result; back-calculate the base by undoing the operation (subtract 5, divide by 3).

question: In a certain code language, 'FLOOR' is coded as '198' and 'GATE' is coded as '99'. How will 'HALL' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 99.

GIVEN

• FLOOR = 198, GATE = 99. Find HALL.

SOLUTION

• Rule: (sum of letter positions) × 3.

• FLOOR = 6+12+15+15+18 = 66; 66×3 = 198. ✓

• GATE = 7+1+20+5 = 33; 33×3 = 99. ✓

• HALL = 8+1+12+12 = 33; 33×3 = 99.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Add letter values, multiply by 3: HALL sum 33 → 99.

NOTE

• Test 'sum of positions × k' for numeric word codes; find k from a given word, then reuse it.

question: In a certain coded language 'LEGGY' is coded as 'MGLET' and 'TOUGH' is coded as 'UQZEC'. How will 'FISTS' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. GKXRN.

GIVEN

• LEGGY = MGLET, TOUGH = UQZEC. Find FISTS.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts are +1, +2, +5, −2, −5.

• Check TOUGH: T+1=U, O+2=Q, U+5=Z, G−2=E, H−5=C → UQZEC. ✓

• FISTS: F+1=G, I+2=K, S+5=X, T−2=R, S−5=N → GKXRN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the shift pattern +1,+2,+5,−2,−5 letter by letter to FISTS → GKXRN.

NOTE

• For coded words find the shift for each position from a verified word, then apply the same positional shifts.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

WP50, TK100, QF200, MZ400, KV800, HQ1600
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. MZ400.

GIVEN

• WP50, TK100, QF200, MZ400, KV800, HQ1600

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: W, T, Q, ?, K, H → step −3 (23,20,17,14=N,11,8). The 4th should be N, not M.

• 2nd letters: P, K, F, ?, V, Q → step −5 (16,11,6,1=A,22,17). The 4th should be A, not Z.

• Numbers double correctly (50,100,200,400,800,1600).

• So the 4th term should be NA400; the given MZ400 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters run W,T,Q,N,K,H (−3 each) — M breaks the chain, so MZ400 is the odd term.

NOTE

• In 'one-wrong' cluster series check each letter column's constant step and the number pattern separately.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

MAN32, PFU48, TJB72, VPI108, YUP162, BZW243
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. TJB72.

GIVEN

• MAN32, PFU48, TJB72, VPI108, YUP162, BZW243

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: M, P, ?, V, Y, B → step +3 (13,16,19=S,22,25,28→B). The 3rd should be S, not T.

• 2nd letters: A, F, ?, P, U, Z → step +5 (1,6,11=K,16,21,26). The 3rd should be K, not J.

• 3rd letters: N,U,B,I,P,W → step +7 (correct). Numbers ×1.5 (32,48,72,108,162,243 — correct).

• So the 3rd term should be SKB72; the given TJB72 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters should read M,P,S,V,Y,B (+3 each) — T breaks it, so TJB72 is the wrong term.

NOTE

• Verify every column's step; only the letters (not the ×1.5 numbers) are off here, exposing the faulty term.
